step1_figure.description: Figure 26.19 shows a fully-differential cascode differential amplifier using NMOS differential input pairs with NMOS cascode transistors and PMOS cascode current-mirror active loads, biased by the beta-multiplier bias circuit from Fig. 26.3. The amplifier's DC transfer curve and gain characteristics are analyzed in Fig. 26.21 on page 878.

differential_voltage_gain.description: Small-signal differential DC voltage gain d(vop - vom)/d(Vinp) at the common-mode quiescent point

equation.formula: A_v = g_mn * (r_on,casc || r_op,casc) ≈ g_mn * [(g_mn * r_on^2) || (g_mp * r_op^2)]
equation.explanation: Differential gain of the cascode differential amplifier is given by the input transconductance multiplied by the output impedance of the NMOS cascode and PMOS cascode load in parallel.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent bias at VCM = 500 mV, devices in saturation with open-circuit gains g_m * r_o ≈ 5 to 10.

sky130_expected.calculation: With (W/L)n = 10u/1u and ID ≈ 10 uA: gmn ≈ sqrt(2 * unCox * (W/L) * ID) = sqrt(2 * 270u * 10 * 10u) ≈ 232 uS. Channel length modulation lambda ≈ 0.1 V^-1, ron ≈ 1/(lambda * ID) = 1/(0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm. Cascode output impedance R_out ≈ 100 kOhm to 300 kOhm in presence of subthreshold/triode margins. The textbook states Av ≈ 40 (32 dB). For SKY130 with VDD=1.8V, Av ≈ 35 to 55 (31 dB to 35 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The textbook directly reports a gain of approximately 40 (32 dB) on page 878, which is typical for a single-stage cascode diff-amp operating at high speed.

output_common_mode_voltage.description: Quiescent output common-mode voltage (vop + vom)/2 when Vinp = VCM = 500 mV

equation.explanation: The DC output voltage of the cascode diff-amp is set around Vbiasp by the PMOS active load mirror reference.
equation.assumptions: Balanced input voltages Vinp = VCM = 500 mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: In the textbook (VDD=1.0V), Vbiasp ≈ 600 mV. For the SKY130 PDK operating at VDD=1.8V, the beta-multiplier generates Vbiasp ≈ VDD - |Vthp| - Vovp ≈ 1.8V - 0.6V = 1.1V to 1.2V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The outputs settle near the PMOS bias voltage Vbiasp established by the self-biasing cascode load.

common_mode_voltage_gain.description: Common-mode gain A_v,cm = d(v_out,cm) / d(V_in,cm) showing output CM sensitivity to input CM variation

equation.explanation: Measures how much the output DC voltage shifts when the common-mode input voltage is changed.
equation.assumptions: VCM varied around nominal 500 mV by ±100 mV.

sky130_expected.calculation: Textbook page 877 states: 'A 200 mV change in the common-mode voltage results in a, roughly, 50 mV change in the diff-amp's common-mode output voltages.' Hence A_v,cm ≈ 50 mV / 200 mV = 0.25 (-12 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The diff-amp without an active CMFB loop relies only on the tail current source output impedance, yielding attenuation around 0.25 (-12 dB).

equation.explanation: Ratio of the differential gain to common-mode gain.
equation.assumptions: Linear small-signal operation around quiescent bias.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Derived directly from textbook differential gain of 40 and common-mode gain of 0.25.

differential_output_swing.description: Maximum peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing (vop - vom)

equation.explanation: Limits on output swing imposed by cascode stack saturation requirements.
equation.assumptions: All NMOS and PMOS cascode devices remain in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VDD = 1.8V and Vds,sat ≈ 150 mV per transistor (4 saturation drops): single-ended range is from ~0.3V to 1.5V (1.2 Vpp). Differential peak-to-peak output swing is 2 * 1.2V ≈ 2.4 Vpp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Differential doubling allows nearly twice the single-ended headroom minus the cascode overdrive voltages.

total_quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD by the diff-amp core and bias generator

equation.explanation: Total current is the sum of the bias circuit reference currents plus the four vertical diff-amp branches.
equation.assumptions: VCM = Vinp = 500 mV, balanced operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: Each of the 4 vertical diff-amp branches carries ~10 uA (total core current ~40 uA). The SUB_1 beta-multiplier bias circuit pulls ~30 uA to 40 uA. Total supply current IDD ≈ 70 uA to 90 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard branch biasing at 10/1 NMOS with 400 mV gate-source overdrive yields ~10 uA per device.

step3_testbench.description: Ngspice testbench characterizing the fully-differential cascode diff-amp of Fig 26.19 in SKY130: measures DC differential gain, quiescent output common-mode voltage, differential output swing, input common-mode gain, CMRR, and DC quiescent supply current.
